column1: # Captured audit-4.0.3, RHEL 10.2, kernel 6.12.0-211, 2026-11-12. After auditctl -D, rule A then rule B loaded with auditctl.
# audit-3.1.5 (Rocky 9.8, kernel 5.14) gave the same exit status and the same printed listing for every row.
# name\tA\tB\tB exit status\tB error ("Rule exists" means one kernel rule; "-" for none)

column2: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -C uid!=euid -F auid!=unset -k c1
column3: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -C euid!=uid -F auid!=unset -k c2

column2: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -C uid!=euid -F euid=root -k k1
column3: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -C uid!=euid -F euid=0 -k k1
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S all -F path=/etc/shadow -F perm=wa -k k1
